'''John Philip Grime''' {{post-nominals|FRS}}<ref name=frs/> (30{{nbsp}}April 1935{{snd}}19{{nbsp}}April 2021)<ref name=rspobit>{{Cite journal|last1=Pierce|first1=Simon|last2=Fridley|first2=Jason D.|date=2021|title=John Philip Grime 30 April 1935 — 19 April 2021|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=71|pages=249–270 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2021.0021 |s2cid=239700780 |doi-access=free}}</ref> was an ecologist and [[emeritus professor]] at the [[University of Sheffield]].<ref name="archive.org">{{cite web|url=http://shef.ac.uk/aps/staff/acadstaff/pgrime.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071013093849/http://shef.ac.uk/aps/staff/acadstaff/pgrime.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=13 October 2007|title=Academic Staff & Independent Research Fellows|date=13 October 2007|access-date=22 April 2019}}</ref> He is best known for the [[universal adaptive strategy theory (UAST)]] and the twin filter model of community assembly with [[Simon Pierce]], [[eco-evolutionary dynamics]], the [[unimodal]] relationship between species richness and site productivity ("humped-back model"), the [[intermediate disturbance hypothesis]], and DST classification (dominants, subordinates and transients).<ref name=sciencewatch>{{Cite web| last = Moore | first = Peter| date = July 1996 <!-- July/August 1996-->| title = University of Sheffield's Philip Grime: Strategic Advances in Plant Ecology| url = http://www.sciencewatch.com/interviews/philip_grime.htm| website = Science Watch| publisher = [[Thomson Scientific]]| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071117062252/http://www.sciencewatch.com/interviews/philip_grime.htm| archive-date = 17 November 2007| access-date = 21 November 2021 }}</ref>

Grime's 1979 book ''Plant Strategies and Vegetation Processes''<ref name=plantstrat/><ref name=plantstrat2/> has been cited more than 1,200 times.{{Citation needed|date=November 2022}} Together with many influential scientific papers, it has made him a highly cited scientist.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://highlycited.com/categories/ecology_environment/|title=Ecology/Environment category list|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111204141205/http://highlycited.com/categories/ecology_environment/|archive-date=4 December 2011|publisher=[[ISIHighlyCited.com]]|access-date=18 May 2012}}</ref> In an interview Grime has stated that "Ecology lacks a Periodic Table", quoting [[Richard Southwood]].<ref name=sciencewatch/>

==Education==
Grime obtained his PhD from [[University of Sheffield]] in 1960.<ref name="archive.org"/>

==Career and research==
Grime joined the staff of the department of [[botany]] at Sheffield in 1961. He worked at the [[Connecticut Agricultural Experiment Station]], US from 1963 to 1964. He then returned to the [[University of Sheffield]] and joined the unit of comparative [[plant ecology]], which had been founded in 1961 by professor Ian H. Rorison.{{citation needed|date=April 2019}} Grime served as deputy director of the Natural Environmental Research Council Unit of Comparative Plant Ecology from 1964 to 1989 and as director from 1989.<ref name="Nature Ecology">{{cite journal|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41559-021-01480-6|title=J. Philip Grime (1935-2021)|author=Ken Thompson, Sandra Díaz|date=17 May 2021|journal=Nature Ecology & Evolution|volume=5 |issue=7 |pages=890–891 |doi=10.1038/s41559-021-01480-6 |bibcode=2021NatEE...5..890T |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

===Plant strategies===
His work and his theories are focused on plant strategies, as developed along their evolutionary history. His CSR theory says that each plant species has a blend of the three strategies that he labels '''C''' (competitive), '''S''' (stress tolerant) and '''R''' (ruderal, or rapid propagation). Ruderal strategists thrive in disturbed areas.<ref name=shape>{{cite book|last1=Grime|first1=J. Philip|last2=Pierce|first2=Simon|title=The Evolutionary Strategies that Shape Ecosystems.|date=30 April 2012|publisher=Wiley-Blackwell|location=Chichester, UK|isbn=978-0-470-67481-9}}</ref> He has described a method to classify herbaceous vegetations by analysing the importance of the three strategies in the genotypes of the species that are present.<ref name=veg>{{cite journal|last=Grime|first=J. Philip|title=Vegetation classification by reference to strategies|journal=Nature|volume=250|date=1974|issue=5461|pages=26–31|doi=10.1038/250026a0|bibcode=1974Natur.250...26G|s2cid=4189430}} {{closed access}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
In 1991, Grime was inducted as a foreign member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/4178 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160130002046/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/4178 |title=J.P. Grime |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |archive-date=30 January 2016 |access-date=29 January 2016}}</ref> In 1997, he won the Marsh Ecology Award from the [[British Ecological Society]] and was awarded honorary membership of the [[Ecological Society of America]]. He was also Distinguished Visiting Ecologist at [[Pennsylvania State University]] in that year. In 1998, he was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS)<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/philip-grime-11546/|title=Philip Grime – Royal Society|website=Royalsociety.org|access-date=22 April 2019}}</ref> and [[honorary doctor]] at [[University of Nijmegen]]. He has been honorary member of the [[British Ecological Society]] since 1999. He was the first ever recipient of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Medal]] (2011) for his outstanding contribution to the intellectual development of plant community ecology.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.iavs.org/uploads/PG-Pres.pdf |year=2011 |title=Alexander von Humboldt Medal J. Philip Grime |first=Jason | last=Fridley}}</ref>

In 2013, the ''[[Journal of Ecology]]'' published a collection of Grime's most influential papers, for which he wrote a blog post and recorded an accompanying [[podcast]] interview.<ref name=frs/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.journalofecology.org/view/0/virtualIssues/jpgrimevi.html|title=In Honour of J Philip Grime – Journal of Ecology|website=Journalofecology.org|doi=10.1111/(ISSN)1365-2745|access-date=22 April 2019}}</ref>
